newsitem.title: UK: S&P gives BBB to Levi Strauss notes, corp credit.
newsitem.headline: S&P gives BBB to Levi Strauss notes, corp credit.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Friday it assigned its BBB rating to Levi Strauss & Co.'s $350 million notes due 2003 and $450 million notes due 2006.
The corporate credit rating is BBB. Proceeds will be used to repay existing debt, S&P said.
The outlook is positive, S&P said.

"The rating reflects the company's well recognized brand name, strong position in the U.S. and international jeans markets, and good cash flow generation. These factors are offset somewhat by LS&Co.'s significant $3.3 billion debt burden following the April 1996 acquisition of Levi Strauss Associates Inc. (LSAI) by LSAI Holdings and the competitive nature of the apparel industry.

LS&Co. holds the number-two market share in the U.S. jeans market due to the ongoing success of its core Levi's brand. Sales of the non-jeans casual Dockers line provide diversification, but have been weak in 1996 because of a higher volume of close outs. Management has refocused and updated the product line, which should result in improved performance over the near term.

The company is the jeans market leader internationally, and total international sales accounted for about 39% of sales and about one-half of operating profit in 1995. International operations are highly profitable due to LS&Co.'s jeans positioning as a more fashionable, premium priced product in most overseas markets.

Historical operating margins in the 17%-18% range are favorable for the apparel industry. Operating margins likely will be constrained over the near term as the company invests in its Customer Service Initiative program to improve distribution capabilities and increase operating efficiencies. Over the intermediate term, operating results should benefit from an improved cost structure and strengthened retailer relationships.

Leverage increased significantly following the 1996 transaction as evidenced by total debt to EBITDA of 3.2 times (x) as of Aug. 25, 1996, and is expected to decline as cash flow is anticipated to be applied to bank debt reduction, rapidly reducing total debt outstanding. Funds from operations to total debt in the 20% range is appropriate for the rating. Cash flow generation is strong as a result of good profitability and moderate working capital and capital expenditures. Standard & Poor's expects discretionary cash flow to be in the $400 million-$500 million range annually over the next few years.

Ratings could be raised within the next couple of years if LS&Co. continues to generate good profitability and significantly reduces debt levels, Standard & Poor's said. -- CreditWire Contact: Pamela E. Gelles, New York (1) 212-208-1355. Reply to tlx 7608140 via CCI."
